title: Experimental evidence for quantum Brownian motion in electron-metal decoherence
authors: Wayne Cheng-Wei Huang, Zilin Chen, Herman Batelaan
abstract: Feynman once remarked that the double-slit experiment has in its heart the only mystery of quantum mechanics. Arguably, the scientific significance of double-slit experiments lies in motional decoherence and the mechanism behind it. Decoherence of motional states underpins our understanding of quantum-to-classical transition. It is also central to the operation of miniaturized quantum electron devices and poses a resolution limit for electron microscopes. In this work, we provide experimental evidence for the critical role of quantum Brownian motion in electron motional decoherence. We demonstrate, for the first time, clear signatures of electron-metal decoherence and its continuous tunability. Our experiment concludes a two-decade long search for experimental realization of the Anglin-Paz-Zurek proposal, establishing electron-microchannel systems as viable open quantum platforms for free-electron quantum optics. The quantitative agreement between experiment and theory further paves the way for testing the Caldeira-Leggett quantum dissipation theory with free electrons.
summary: This research experimentally verifies the role of quantum Brownian motion in decohering electron wave packets as they interact with metal surfaces. By employing electron diffractometers, the authors measure decoherence rates with unprecedented tunability. This establishes free-electron systems as a viable, controllable platform for studying fundamental open quantum dynamics.
main_problem: The paper investigates the critical role of quantum Brownian motion in causing decoherence of electron motional states as they interact with metallic surfaces.
main_result: The authors provide clear experimental signatures of electron-metal decoherence and demonstrate its continuous tunability using electron diffractometers, confirming the theoretical predictions of the Anglin-Paz-Zurek proposal.
method: The experiment uses electron diffractometers to measure intra-beam decoherence, contrasting this with traditional inter-beam interferometry setups.
model_or_system: The system involves an electron beam passing near a gold-plated microchannel, where decoherence arises from entanglement between the electron's position and image charges induced by the metal surface, governed by quantum Brownian motion theory (Caldeira-Leggett).
key_observables: Fringe visibility ($V$) loss, homogeneous width broadening in diffraction patterns, and the decoherence rate ($\gamma_{dec}$)
important_parameters: Electron-surface distance ($y$), effective interaction strength ($\Delta t/y^3$), and the microchannel tilt angle ($	heta$)
main_assumptions: The use of diffractometers is assumed to effectively isolate intra-beam decoherence from spurious effects that plague single-beam measurements.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the link between classical and quantum Brownian motion, compare decoherence detection in inter-beam vs. intra-beam setups, and show the experimental setup using the microchannel.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical background (APZ proposal, quantum Brownian motion), details the experimental setup using electron diffractometers, presents measurements showing tunable decoherence rates, and concludes by validating the theory against experimental data.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses open quantum systems by providing a measurable platform (free-electron quantum optics) to test fundamental dissipation theories like Caldeira-Leggett, which is highly relevant to understanding decoherence mechanisms in quantum devices.
